name: Komyandaret
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only survey wordlist (Hughes 2009 Upper Digul Survey); no grammar or phonology exists

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2012 Part I: 269-312.
sources.note: Classification only (Becking-Dawi: Korowai, North Korowai, Tsaukambo, Komyandaret); no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent'.
Bibliographic only; sole descriptive ref is Hughes 2009.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2020. The Greater Awyu Languages of West Papua in Typological Perspective. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Ch. 2 phonology treats Aghu, Digul Wambon, Kombai, Korowai only. On Becking-Dawi: 'Korowai is the only language in this group for which there is a grammar.. For the other languages we only have field notes and word lists. Komyandaret is a dialect of Tsaukambo according to Baas (1981)'. Komyandaret appears otherwise only in a pronoun table (nonu, gonu, ye, nau, gagu). Nothing on Komyandaret stress.

sources.citation: Wester, Ruth. 2014. A linguistic history of Awyu-Dumut: morphological study and reconstruction of a Papuan language family. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.note: Sec. 1.1.13 Komyandaret: 'Almost no linguistic data on Komyandaret exist, except for a 239-item word list in the 2009 SIL survey.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2012. Some notes on the Tsaukambo language of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2012 Part I: 165-193.
sources.note: On Tsaukambo (of which Komyandaret is a near-identical variety per Baas 1981:90, sec. 5.1): p.166 'There are not enough data in the field notes to enable a phonological analysis' (only syllable types, examples stress-marked [me'li], [nama'ka], [æ'nɔ]); later 'We need much more data, on stress patterns and vowel variation'. No stress rule for Tsaukambo or Komyandaret; Komyandaret data limited to Hughes's wordlist.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-003. Dallas: SIL International. 43 pp.
sources.note: Nothing stated. Sociolinguistic survey; 'KOMYANDARET' section printed pp. 7-8 (p. 12) covers name, village, lexical similarity (60% with Tsaukambo), language use. Appendix V (pp. 32-43) prints a 239-item 'Komyandaret / Donokit' wordlist in IPA with primary-stress marks (e.g. 001 head ʔæˈbjæ, 003 eye ɸɔˈjɔ, 005 nose ɢəˈli, 036 jɑˈmɔdɔʔ, 048 ˈkəjæˌnɔʔ) but gives no rule or comment on stress placement.

sources.citation: OLAC / SIL Language & Culture Archives holdings for ISO kzv (Komyandaret) and kvz (Tsaukambo), incl. any unpublished SIL-Indonesia survey wordlist recordings from the 2000 Upper Digul survey.

sources.note: Nearest described relative (same Becking-Dawi branch): 'Stress is unpredictable and therefore phonemic' — relevant comparandum only, not a Komyandaret source.

sources.citation: Baas, Peter. 1981. Tsakwambo field notebook (unpublished, 235 pp; ZGK mission, Kawagit; pp. 129-178 texts in IPA, wordlists and language notes). Excerpted in de Vries 2012.

sources.note: Only other primary material on Tsaukambo, of which Baas treats Komyandaret as a variety; IPA texts might carry stress marks, though de Vries (2012:166) judged the notes insufficient for phonological analysis.
